clue.text: Brilliant disc for John, Paul, or George, perhaps

parts.words: Brilliant disc for John, Paul, or George, perhaps
parts.note: surface reading: a hit record by three of the Beatles

parts.words: for John, Paul, or George, perhaps
parts.note: setter's reading: these are saints' names, and saints are painted with a shining ring above the head

explanation.surface: A dazzling record by one of the Beatles.
explanation.walkthrough: The names steer you to the Beatles and a gold disc, but they are meant as saints: Saint John, Saint Paul, Saint George.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is the bright circle of light shown around the head of a saint in religious art.

clue.text: They never oppose head of state in part of Middle East

indicators.note: one item placed in another means it goes inside that word

parts.note: a country on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: 'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'state'

parts.note: the first letter of state

explanation.surface: A description of courtiers who never contradict a Gulf ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who always agree with whoever is in charge, never opposing them.

clue.text: Beginner from county losing couple of points, finally

indicators.note: losing tells you letters are dropped from the county name
finally places the lost letters at the very end of the word

parts.note: Tyrone is a county of Northern Ireland
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A novice who comes from a county and fumbles a couple of points at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a novice, someone just starting to learn a skill.

clue.text: Aid to meditation used by shaman, traditionally

indicators.note: the letters wanted are used by, so held within, the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A shaman's traditional technique for helping meditation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or sound repeated to help concentration during meditation.

clue.text: Festive drinking in clubs leading to excitement

indicators.note: one part leading to another means it comes first, with the next following

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a synonym: stirring up of feeling

explanation.surface: Holiday boozing in nightclubs leads to wild excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a noisy, merry drinking party, the activity of carousing.

clue.text: Possible murder clue misrepresented in tabloids? No

indicators.note: misrepresented means presented wrongly, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: all ten letters are used

explanation.surface: Was evidence in a murder case twisted by the popular press? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'No' read as a comment, but 'No' supplies two of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodstain at a scene is the kind of physical evidence that may point to a killing.

clue.text: Absurd probe into salary for one who delivers

indicators.note: going into another word means sitting inside it

parts.note: a synonym for wages

indicators.note: something absurd makes no sense as it stands, so the word is jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A ridiculous inquiry into the wages paid to a delivery worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperboy delivers newspapers to homes, so he is one who delivers.

clue.text: Single-handedly cutting through claptrap

indicators.note: one word cutting another slices into it, ending up inside

parts.note: by means via or through, as in travelling by a town
doing something single-handedly is doing it without help

explanation.surface: Someone hacking their way through nonsense with no help at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloney is informal for nonsense, as is claptrap: empty, foolish talk.

clue.text: Drink outside pub put back, ready for ploughperson

indicators.note: one word outside another wraps around it

parts.note: a type of beer

indicators.note: putting something back here means writing it in the opposite direction

parts.note: a synonym for a pub

explanation.surface: A drink is placed outside a pub, ready for a farmer finishing ploughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is suitable for ploughing and growing crops.

clue.text: A learner comes after class, according to convention

indicators.note: one part coming after another means it is written to its right

parts.note: a form is a school class, especially in Britain
taken as written
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student joins the class later than the others, as is customary.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal describes doing things by established rules and etiquette, so following convention.

clue.text: Steer behind modified hot rod, following usual practice

indicators.note: behind places one part after the other in the answer
something modified has been changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a steer is a castrated bull, as is an ox

explanation.surface: Someone steering behind a customised car, as is the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Steer looks like a verb about driving the hot rod, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means conforming to accepted rules or established practice.

clue.text: Kind of education that's levelling out social differences?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: adult courses held after the working day
second meaning, playful: making the social ranks equal, read as a verb phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun in the second half: 'evening' is read as the verb 'making even', and 'classes' as social ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-school courses for adults are a recognised kind of education; read as a phrase, the words also mean equalising social strata.

clue.text: Damaged museum slide replaced

parts.note: the V and A, London's Victoria and Albert Museum

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A slide in a museum display got broken and had to be swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandalised means deliberately damaged, as by vandals.

clue.text: Triumphantly elevate academic position

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to carry a winner aloft on shoulders
second meaning: a professorship at a university

explanation.surface: Celebrating a promotion to a prestigious university post.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a hero is to hoist them on shoulders; a chair is also a professor's post.

clue.text: Realise it can be perceived as negative by audience

indicators.note: perceived here means taken in by the ear, so the sound counts rather than the spelling
an audience is a group of listeners, so what matters is how the word is heard

parts.note: no is the word of refusal; the answer is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Accepting that something may be received badly by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by audience' completes the indicator: it is the listeners who perceive it.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a fact is to become aware of it, to know it.

clue.text: Made dry red, inferior to white, oddly

indicators.note: inferior means lower, and in a down answer lower means placed after
oddly means in a strange way, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dry red wine strangely judged worse than the white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts you to take alternate letters of white, but here it means scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Withered means shrivelled and dried up, as a plant losing moisture.

clue.text: Poet sharing food with Keats, but with different starter

indicators.note: a different starter means the opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: eats is informal for food
the Romantic poet, whose name ends in the same four letters

explanation.surface: One poet sharing a meal with Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: The two poets share the ending EATS; replace Keats's K with a new first letter to reach another famous poet, W B Yeats.
explanation.definitionFit: W B Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Champion leading in golf, say

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: golf is an example of a sport
a player who is leading is up, ahead in the match

explanation.surface: A golf champion leading the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Champion is a verb here, to back a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support it, standing up for it.

clue.text: Clue recurring in puzzle, a debatable addition

indicators.note: something recurring in a passage appears within it, so look inside the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A doubtful clue that keeps turning up in a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is a clue or hint in an investigation that points toward a solution.

clue.text: Parent is, in part, changing requirement for sweater

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all fourteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A parent partly changing what's needed for a knitted jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweater suggests a woolly jumper, but here it is a person who sweats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sweats needs a deodorant product that reduces perspiration.

clue.text: Part of seven-piece suite's in flat on time

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Part of a seven-piece furniture set sitting in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: The suite is not furniture: Holst's orchestral suite The Planets has seven movements, each named after a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Each movement of Holst's The Planets portrays one world of the solar system, such as Mars or Jupiter.

clue.text: Improvement coming from cure for malady

indicators.note: coming from means emerging out of the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Health improving thanks to a remedy for an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A reform is a change that makes something better, an improvement.

clue.text: Misprints in American volume too unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is left off

parts.note: the American spelling of litre, a measure of volume
a synonym meaning as well

explanation.surface: Typos found in an incomplete American book.
explanation.walkthrough: Volume looks like a book, but it is the unit of capacity, spelt the American way.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, literals are typographical errors, single-letter mistakes.

clue.text: How deal is cut, having spotted what's on top of charts

parts.note: past tense of see
north is at the top of maps and charts

explanation.surface: A business deal reduced after seeing what tops the music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is the timber of fir or pine, not an agreement; charts are maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal planks are sawn, cut with a saw, so this is how the wood is cut.

clue.text: Backed party about vote favouring university

indicators.note: about means going around something else
backed means turned to face the other way, so read the word right to left

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper
being for something is favouring it

explanation.surface: A supported political party ran a poll that favoured a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is the name of England's oldest university.

clue.text: Cheat man on board initially trapped in corner

definitions.text: man on board initially trapped in corner
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a chess piece that begins the game in a corner square

explanation.surface: A swindler first cornered and caught on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Initially means at the start of the game, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to defraud; the rook is the chess piece starting in each corner of the board.

clue.text: Cut off energy — that's hard to endure

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Having the power cut off is a real hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe hardship or pain is intense and difficult to bear.

clue.text: Unusually alert in court battle

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly watchful during a fight in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo was the 1815 battle where Napoleon was finally defeated.
